text:
sophia: quick design check — pushed two variants for the regression-diff heatmap hover and approve CTA placement. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/regs-diff
mike: skimmed. Variant B (sticky micro-toolbar) feels more discoverable on long diffs. contrast on hover looks low though.
ana: agree re: contrast. also noticed keyboard focus outline disappears in compact mode.
jon: can you paste the css you're using for the sticky toolbar? curious about potential reflow.
priya: a11y note: focus ring must remain visible and meet 3:1 contrast. also prefer text label for CTA vs icon-only for screen readers.
sophia: two quick options: A) inline CTA in diff header, B) sticky micro-toolbar that appears when you scroll. i updated proto with focus state and longer label on B.
mike: sticky is better for discoverability but will overlap content on small viewports. maybe show sticky only on >= 1024px.
ana: responsive reveal sounds right. also tooltips must be keyboard accessible, not hover-only.
jon: impl note — use transform-based stickiness to reduce layout shift (avoid toggling top/height). also need aria-live when diffs change while toolbar is sticky.
priya: keyboard flow: ensure approve remains reachable in tab order when toolbar becomes sticky. don't reorder DOM focus sequence.
sophia: added tooltip copy: `Approve changes (shortcut: a)` and visible label for screen readers.
ana: tooltip ok but confirm it appears on focus. add `role="tooltip"` and tie to `aria-describedby`.
mike: performance flag — sticky on many diffs could cause jank. limit to first visible diff or render a single sticky instance.
jon: CSS snippet suggestion:
```
.sticky-toolbar { position: sticky; top: 0; transform: translateZ(0); will-change: transform; }
```
keeps paint cheap.
sophia: thanks — i'll try that approach and measure CLS.
design-bot: accessibility-scan: Variant B button hover fails contrast on dark theme (#2 issues).
priya: change CTA text from `Approve` to `Approve changes` for clarity and analytics; keep `aria-label` short on micro variants.
ana: tiny nit — on very compact diffs the approve icon should be 44x44 touch target even if visual size smaller.
mike: can we do 3 quick usability calls (15m) to validate discoverability? i'll book tomorrow morning and tag people.
sophia: perfect — i'll update figma + open a PR with css + unit tests for focus state. tagging @mike for the usability slot :calendar:
